timeline.label: Q1 2026 balance sheet shows $63.1B total debt and lease obligations and $9.8B cash; debt fact refreshed for universal contract.
FY2025 10-K filed: revenue $402.1B, operating cash flow $10.6B, capital spending $2.8B.
FY2025 normalized owner earnings $7.8B (operating cash flow minus capital spending) anchors reinvestment DCF.
David Joyner became President and CEO; Karen Lynch transitioned to Executive Chair, reshaping capital allocation focus after Medicare Advantage headwinds.
Medicare Advantage star-rating and reimbursement pressure weighed on Health Care Benefits margins; management guided to margin recovery programs.
Completed Signify Health acquisition, expanding value-based care and in-home services within the integrated model.
Closed Oak Street Health acquisition, adding primary-care clinics aligned with Medicare Advantage membership.
Closed Aetna acquisition, creating integrated PBM, retail pharmacy, and health-insurance platform.
Pharmacy reimbursement compression and generic deflation cycle pressured retail pharmacy margins industry-wide.
Omnicare and Target pharmacy acquisitions expanded long-term care and retail pharmacy footprint.

industry.structure: Highly concentrated U.S. healthcare services: three major PBMs, national retail pharmacy chains, and large Medicare Advantage insurers; scale, formulary control, and retail density create barriers but reimbursement is politically sensitive.
industry.share_shift: CVS, UnitedHealth, and Cigna/Evernorth compete on integrated care and PBM scale; independent pharmacies lose share to chains; Medicare Advantage enrollment growth slows as star ratings and medical costs bite.
industry.trend: GLP-1 utilization, specialty drug mix, Medicare Advantage margin repair, and site-of-care shifts (retail clinics, home health) dominate; leverage and integration synergies remain the bull case against reimbursement headwinds.
